quickSummary: The flower is a condensed reproductive shoot with accessory (calyx, corolla) and essential (androecium, gynoecium) whorls. Symmetry is actinomorphic (radial, Mustard) or zygomorphic (bilateral, Pea). Thalamus insertion dictates ovary position: Hypogynous (superior ovary), Perigynous (half-inferior, Rose/Peach), and Epigynous (inferior ovary, Guava/Cucumber/Sunflower).

conceptBreakdown.content: The flower is a complex, highly modified, condensed reproductive shoot designed for sexual reproduction. It is borne on a stalk called a **Pedicel**, ending in a swollen apex called the **Thalamus / Receptacle**.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.1 Floral Symmetry Types
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.1 Floral Symmetry Types
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Actinomorphic ($\oplus$)**: Radial symmetry; flower can be divided into equal halves in any vertical radial plane passing through the center (*Mustard*, *Datura*, *Chilli*).
• **Zygomorphic ($\%$)**: Bilateral symmetry; flower can be divided into equal halves in only **one single median vertical plane** (*Pea*, *Gulmohar*, *Cassia*, *Bean*).
• **Asymmetric**: Cannot be divided into identical halves along any vertical plane (*Canna*).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.2 Insertion of Floral Whorls on Thalamus (Ovary Position)
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.2 Insertion of Floral Whorls on Thalamus (Ovary Position)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
OVARY INSERTION ARCHITECTURE
                       
    HYPOGYNOUS (\underline{G})         PERIGYNOUS (G- )           EPIGYNOUS (\bar{G})
    ├── Superior Ovary               ├── Half-Inferior Ovary           ├── Inferior Ovary
    ├── Thalamus conical/convex      ├── Thalamus cup-like rim         ├── Thalamus completely encloses
    └── Calyx/Corolla inserted       └── Calyx/Corolla inserted            ovary & fuses with it
        BELOW ovary                      AT THE MARGIN LEVEL           └── Whorls inserted ABOVE
    ├── *Mustard*, *Brinjal*,        ├── *Plum*, *Rose*,               ├── *Guava*, *Cucumber*,
        *China rose*                     *Peach*                           Ray florets of *Sunflower*
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Hypogynous ($\mathbf{\underline{G}}$)**: The gynoecium occupies the highest position on a convex or conical thalamus while the calyx, corolla, and stamens are inserted below it. The ovary is **Superior** (*Mustard*, *China rose*, *Brinjal*).
2. **Perigynous ($\mathbf{G-}$)**: The gynoecium is situated in the center, and other floral parts are located on the rim/margin of a cup-shaped or saucer-shaped thalamus at almost the same level. The ovary is **Half-Inferior** (*Plum*, *Rose*, *Peach*).
3. **Epigynous ($\mathbf{\bar{G}}$)**: The margin of the thalamus grows upward enclosing the ovary completely and getting fused with it; the calyx, corolla, and stamens arise above the ovary. The ovary is **Inferior** (*Guava*, *Cucumber*, and ray florets of *Sunflower*).
